description: The proof a server sends in its hello, from the token, the client's nonce and the server's PID. Each invalid proof is well formed but computed from the mistaken input its flag names.

notes.GeneratedToken: The token is 32 random bytes encoded as base64url, as a generated token is, and its key is still its text.
notes.UserToken: The token is one a user gave, in ASCII with spaces and punctuation.
notes.MultiByteToken: The token holds 2-, 3- and 4-byte UTF-8 characters, so a key made from anything but its UTF-8 bytes differs.
notes.PidRange: The PID is 0 or 4294967295, an end of the unsigned 32-bit range.
notes.WrongLabel: The proof was computed with the enrollment label in place of the hello label.
notes.MissingSeparator: The proof was computed without the 0x00 byte after the label.
notes.PidLittleEndian: The proof was computed with the PID's 4 bytes little-endian.
notes.PidAsText: The proof was computed with the PID as ASCII decimal digits in place of its 4 bytes.
notes.NonceAsText: The proof was computed with the nonce's 43 base64url characters in place of the 32 bytes they decode to.
notes.DecodedTokenKey: The proof was computed with the bytes a generated token decodes to as the key, in place of its UTF-8 text.
notes.RelayedProof: The proof was computed with otherPid in place of the case's PID, as a proof relayed from another server process is.
notes.UntrimmedToken: The token starts and ends with spaces, which are part of its text and so of the key.
notes.TrimmedTokenKey: The proof was computed with the token's leading and trailing spaces trimmed from the key.
